description: Every exact classical route to simulating a program, priced on it: the stabilizer tableau, the cut-rank sum, an exact matrix product state at a rigorous bond bound, the light cone of a one-qubit expectation value, and the state vector. The cheapest is named for each question. A cheap route proves the program classically easy; none being cheap proves nothing about hardness. A thorough search, with a contraction tree, runs locally: wai-quantum shortcuts --thorough.
name: classical_shortcuts

cheapest.description: For counts, amplitudes, expectations and one_qubit_expectations: the cheapest route that answers it, or null.

reference_rate.description: Operations a second the times assume.

verdict.description: How far the engine checked an answer about a program, as one level of an ordered ladder (wai-quantum://docs/verdicts): refused, parsed, executed, evidence, proof. A level says how far the engine checked, not that the answer is good: holds says whether the intents held (true, false, or null when none was decided). A job's result carries one under verdict when the job gives an intent or asks for one, and the receipt seals it; both MCP servers state one beside every answer about a program.
